notes: Amulet Hotkey DXZC is a Teradici Tera2321 PCoIP zero client (remote-desktop endpoint, not a general-purpose PC) — closest catalog fit used is category "source" / type "Computer"; treat as approximate classification since no dedicated "zero client" type exists in the taxonomy. Specs drawn from the manufacturer's own datasheet content (Datasheet DS-DXZC-0001 v2.8, Apr 2018, published by Amulet Hotkey Ltd, mirrored by a distributor as the manufacturer's live datasheet PDF was not directly retrievable over plain HTTPS fetch) and cross-verified against Amulet Hotkey's own current product photography (files DXZC_front*.png / DXZC_rear*.png, uploaded Dec 2025 to www.amulethotkey.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/), which show identical, clearly silkscreen-labeled ports: NETWORK, VIDEO (x2), USB (x2 rear + x2 front), LINE OUT, POWER on the rear, and MIC, HEADSET (H/PHONES), USB (x2) on the front. Port count/labels match the datasheet's stated "2 x DisplayPort (dual mode)", "4 x USB 2.0", "Stereo headset/headphones, stereo line out, stereo mic (3.5mm)", and "Single RJ45: 10/100/1000BaseT" for the base DXZC model. DisplayPort version/generation is not stated in the source, so no grade was set (omitted per instructions). This spec is for the base "DXZC" model with RJ45; sibling variants DXZC-M and DXZC-AM replace the RJ45 network port with an SFP cage (copper or fiber module, 1Gbit/s or 1Mbit/s) — not modeled here since the user asked specifically about "DXZC". Device is a small desktop unit (30 x 176 x 133 mm, 0.6 kg) — not rack-mountable, so rackUnits is omitted. Power connector is visually a small locking multi-pin DIN-style circular jack (confirmed via close-up of the manufacturer photo) rather than a plain cylindrical barrel jack; "dc-barrel" was used as the closest available connector id in the given list.
